# haproxy

[haproxy/haproxy](https://github.com/haproxy/haproxy) · OSS-Fuzz: [projects/haproxy](https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/bd2ce21991a94a362b92fb1bf25f86d5a1a60842/projects/haproxy)

| [fuzz_cfg_parser](fuzz_cfg_parser/) | One-time trash-buffer init, then parse_cfg() on the fuzzed bytes as a whole configuration file (inputs < 50 bytes skipped); the parse result and resulting global state are not inspected. | none | 15 |

| [fuzz_h1_parse](fuzz_h1_parse/) | First byte selects request/response; h1_headers_to_hdr_list over a NUL-terminated copy of the rest into a 101-entry header list; the return value, parsed start line and headers are discarded. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_hpack_decode](fuzz_hpack_decode/) | Allocates a 4096-byte dynamic header table and runs hpack_decode_frame on the fuzzed bytes into a 1000-entry header list; the return code and decoded headers are discarded (no HPACK encode/decode round-trip). | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_http](fuzz_http/) | First byte (mod 7) selects one group of src/http.c helpers: URI scheme/authority/path parsing, Content-Length parsing (twice, to hit duplicate detection), cookie extraction, header/start-line/status parsing, host/port/method/qvalue/etag helpers, URL-parameter search, cookie-value end. All results are discarded. | none | 15 |

## What the statements say, for haproxy
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch haproxy
    ./oft verify-sha haproxy

By hand: download `haproxy-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/haproxy/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [haproxy/haproxy](https://github.com/haproxy/haproxy) at `cb1eebf9d985a2100c6eff4368cde539d89fd845`, built with its own build scripts:
  - 2 patches, whose text is not in this release yet (it ships in the source bundle)
- Harnesses: the harness files are modified in `fuzz_hpack_decode` (see each harness page); the others are unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
